question: A user submits an image and asks open-ended natural-language questions about its scene and relationships. Which approach directly supports this interaction?

options.text: Use speech synthesis
Image classification
Object detection
Send the image and question to a deployed vision-capable multimodal model

explanation: Classification predicts image-level labels, and object detection locates objects. A vision-capable multimodal model supports contextual visual questions.
learningObjective: Interpret visual input in prompts by using a deployed multimodal model

optionExplanations.A: Speech synthesis produces spoken audio from text; it does not inspect the submitted image.
optionExplanations.B: Classification predicts image-level labels rather than answering open-ended questions about scene relationships.
optionExplanations.C: Object detection locates objects but does not by itself provide contextual natural-language question answering.
optionExplanations.D: A vision-capable multimodal model combines the image with the user's question to produce a contextual answer.

question: A design app must produce a revised image based on an uploaded reference and text instructions. Which capability is needed?

options.text: Image classification of the reference photo
Object detection on the reference photo
An image-generation model that supports image input and editing instructions
Text summarization of a description

explanation: Image-generation models can create or edit visual outputs from text and, where supported, reference-image input.
learningObjective: Create new visual outputs by using generative models

optionExplanations.A: This assigns an image-level category rather than locating individual objects; image-generation models can create or edit visual outputs from text and, where supported, reference-image input.
optionExplanations.B: This locates individual objects and can return their bounding boxes; image-generation models can create or edit visual outputs from text and, where supported, reference-image input.
optionExplanations.C: Image-generation models can create or edit visual outputs from text and, where supported, reference-image input.
optionExplanations.D: This condenses source text to its main points; image-generation models can create or edit visual outputs from text and, where supported, reference-image input.

question: A developer wants to validate visual question answering before building a lightweight application. Which test is most useful in Foundry?

options.text: Run an image classifier and review only its label
Upload representative images to a deployed vision-capable model in the playground and test task-specific questions
Test speech synthesis without supplying an image
Inspect the model deployment name without sending a request

explanation: The Foundry playground lets you test a deployed vision-capable model with representative images and text questions before implementing the same request in a client.
learningObjective: Build a lightweight application that includes vision capabilities

optionExplanations.A: This returns an image-level label rather than testing whether a multimodal model answers visual questions; the Foundry playground lets you test a deployed vision-capable model with representative images and text questions before implementing the same request in a client.
optionExplanations.B: The Foundry playground lets you test a deployed vision-capable model with representative images and text questions before implementing the same request in a client.
optionExplanations.C: This converts text into spoken audio; the Foundry playground lets you test a deployed vision-capable model with representative images and text questions before implementing the same request in a client.
optionExplanations.D: This identifies or labels a deployment but does not provide the required model capability by itself; the Foundry playground lets you test a deployed vision-capable model with representative images and text questions before implementing the same request in a client.

question: Which input is most directly associated with the visual-prompt objective?

options.text: Visual input included with a prompt
Only a deployment display name
Only an output-token limit
Only a speech-synthesis voice name

explanation: A visual-prompt request must provide the visual content together with the text instruction; deployment and output settings do not supply the image.
learningObjective: Interpret visual input in prompts by using a deployed multimodal model

optionExplanations.A: A visual-prompt request must provide the visual content together with the text instruction; deployment and output settings do not supply the image.
optionExplanations.B: This identifies or labels a deployment but does not provide the required model capability by itself; a visual-prompt request must provide the visual content together with the text instruction; deployment and output settings do not supply the image.
optionExplanations.C: This caps the amount of generated output rather than changing sampling randomness; a visual-prompt request must provide the visual content together with the text instruction; deployment and output settings do not supply the image.
optionExplanations.D: A synthesis voice name selects audio-output characteristics; it does not supply an image to a vision model.

question: Which capability creates rather than merely interprets visual content?

options.text: Visual interpretation
Speech recognition
Entity extraction
Generative image model

explanation: Generative models can create new visual outputs.
learningObjective: Create new visual outputs by using generative models

optionExplanations.A: This analyzes existing images rather than creating new visual content; generative models can create new visual outputs.
optionExplanations.B: This converts spoken audio into text; generative models can create new visual outputs.
optionExplanations.C: This identifies entities in text rather than interpreting visual input; generative models can create new visual outputs.
optionExplanations.D: Generative models can create new visual outputs.

question: Which TWO requirements respectively call for visual understanding and image generation?

options.text: Transcribe a recording into text
Identify organizations mentioned in written feedback
Answer a text question about an image using a deployed multimodal model
Create a new illustration from a text prompt using an image-generation model

explanation: C interprets existing visual content; D creates new visual content. Image classification and object detection are also computer-vision tasks.
learningObjective: Implement AI solutions with computer vision and image-generation capabilities by using Foundry

optionExplanations.A: Transcription converts speech into text; it neither interprets the supplied image nor creates a new illustration.
optionExplanations.B: Entity recognition identifies named references in text, not visual scenes or new illustrations.
optionExplanations.C: C interprets existing visual content; D creates new visual content.
optionExplanations.D: C interprets existing visual content; D creates new visual content.

question: Match each application requirement to the visual capability that best fits it.

items.text: A camera assigns one label, such as “damaged,” to each whole package image.
An app returns a rectangle around every item on a store shelf.
A customer asks a natural-language question about a submitted photo and its scene.
A marketing tool creates a new banner from a text description.

explanation: Classification assigns image-level labels, detection returns object locations, multimodal models answer contextual questions about images, and generative models create new visuals.
learningObjective: Implement AI solutions with computer vision and image-generation capabilities by using Foundry

question: A multimodal model must answer a question about a chart supplied as an image. What should the request include?

options.text: The chart image and a clear text question
Only the filename of an image stored on the user’s inaccessible local drive
Only a model deployment name
Only an output-token limit

explanation: The model request must include the chart through a supported image reference or encoding and a text question explaining the desired analysis.
learningObjective: Interpret visual input in prompts by using a deployed multimodal model

optionExplanations.A: The model request must include the chart through a supported image reference or encoding and a text question explaining the desired analysis.
optionExplanations.B: This names a file the service cannot access and does not transmit the image data; the model request must include the chart through a supported image reference or encoding and a text question explaining the desired analysis.
optionExplanations.C: This identifies or labels a deployment but does not provide the required model capability by itself; the model request must include the chart through a supported image reference or encoding and a text question explaining the desired analysis.
optionExplanations.D: This caps the amount of generated output rather than changing sampling randomness; the model request must include the chart through a supported image reference or encoding and a text question explaining the desired analysis.

question: You need an image-generation model to create a wide banner without lettering. Which combination of prompt content and request settings is most appropriate?

options.text: Image classification
Object detection
An entity-detection confidence threshold
Describe the subject and composition, request no text, and select a supported wide image size in the request settings

explanation: Prompting guides visual content; supported size settings control output dimensions. Review the generated result because prompt constraints are not a guarantee.
learningObjective: Create new visual outputs by using generative models

optionExplanations.A: This assigns an image-level category rather than locating individual objects; prompting guides visual content; supported size settings control output dimensions.
optionExplanations.B: This locates individual objects and can return their bounding boxes; prompting guides visual content; supported size settings control output dimensions.
optionExplanations.C: This configures text extraction and does not set an image-generation size or prompt; prompting guides visual content; supported size settings control output dimensions.
optionExplanations.D: Prompting guides visual content; supported size settings control output dimensions.

question: A vision-enabled application sends an image to a deployed model. What application requirement is essential?

options.text: Create a Content Understanding audio analyzer
Image classification
Encode or reference the image in a supported request format
Convert the image to speech first

explanation: The client must provide visual content in a request format supported by the deployed multimodal model.
learningObjective: Build a lightweight application that includes vision capabilities

optionExplanations.A: This uses an analyzer and schema to turn supported unstructured content into structured fields; the client must provide visual content in a request format supported by the deployed multimodal model.
optionExplanations.B: This assigns an image-level category rather than locating individual objects; the client must provide visual content in a request format supported by the deployed multimodal model.
optionExplanations.C: The client must provide visual content in a request format supported by the deployed multimodal model.
optionExplanations.D: This adds an unnecessary speech-synthesis step instead of sending the image in a supported model request; the client must provide visual content in a request format supported by the deployed multimodal model.

question: A vision model gives a vague answer about an uploaded image. Which change is most likely to improve the response?

options.text: Ask a specific question about the visual details you need
Remove the image from the request
Replace the prompt with a deployment name
Increase speech synthesis speed

explanation: A specific visual question directs the multimodal model towards the relevant details in the image.
learningObjective: Interpret visual input in prompts by using a deployed multimodal model

optionExplanations.A: A specific visual question directs the multimodal model towards the relevant details in the image.
optionExplanations.B: This removes the visual evidence needed to answer a question about the image; a specific visual question directs the multimodal model towards the relevant details in the image.
optionExplanations.C: This identifies or labels a deployment but does not provide the required model capability by itself; a specific visual question directs the multimodal model towards the relevant details in the image.
optionExplanations.D: Speech synthesis speed changes audio playback timing, not how the model interprets the uploaded image.

question: An image-generation result includes unwanted elements. What is the best first adjustment?

options.text: Switch to speech recognition
Remove all task instructions
Image classification
Refine the prompt with explicit constraints and desired composition

explanation: More explicit constraints and composition guidance usually improve alignment between the prompt and generated image.
learningObjective: Create new visual outputs by using generative models

optionExplanations.A: This converts spoken audio into text; more explicit constraints and composition guidance usually improve alignment between the prompt and generated image.
optionExplanations.B: This removes constraints that guide the requested visual composition; more explicit constraints and composition guidance usually improve alignment between the prompt and generated image.
optionExplanations.C: This assigns an image-level category rather than locating individual objects; more explicit constraints and composition guidance usually improve alignment between the prompt and generated image.
optionExplanations.D: More explicit constraints and composition guidance usually improve alignment between the prompt and generated image.
